problems.title: Match weekdays with odd dates
problems.question: Two cousins are away on even dates. A visitor comes every Monday and Thursday. If the 10th is Friday, how many meetings occur this month?
problems.idea: They meet only when a visit falls on an odd date.
steps: The 1st is Wednesday. Mondays are 6,13,20,27 and Thursdays 2,9,16,23,30 if the month has a 30th.
All four exist even in a 28-day month, so the unspecified month length does not change the result.

problems.title: Possible square remainders modulo 8
problems.question: Which listed remainder 2,3,5,6,7 can a square have modulo 8?
problems.idea: Test the eight possible input residues.
steps: None of the listed five residues occurs.
problems.answer: None of them; square residues are 0,1,4.

problems.title: Reduce an expression before squaring
problems.question: a=6k+1,b=6k+2,c=6k+4. Find the remainder of abc+(ab+bc+ca)² modulo 6.
problems.idea: Replace a,b,c by 1,2,4.

problems.title: Intersection versus symmetric difference
problems.question: Which listed set statement need not hold for arbitrary A,B?
problems.idea: The intersection and symmetric difference contain different kinds of elements.
steps: An element in A∩B belongs to both sets, while one in A△B belongs to exactly one.
Thus A∩B need not be a subset of A△B. For A=B={1}, the first set is {1} and the second empty.
problems.note: The subset symbol is interpreted as allowing equality, the convention used by the other choices. Under a strict-subset convention some other printed statements also fail.

problems.title: Natural numbers are not all even
problems.question: N is the positive natural numbers, K the positive odd integers, L the positive even integers. Which listed assertion is false?
problems.idea: Odd and even positive integers partition N.
steps: Since K is nonempty, N\L cannot be empty.
The other listed partition identities hold.
problems.note: Here natural numbers start at 1. If N included 0, the stated positive sets K,L would also omit that element from their union.

problems.title: Units-digit cycles
problems.question: Find the last digit of 7⁷⁷⁷+14¹⁴¹⁴-3³³³.
problems.idea: Reduce the exponents in the units-digit cycles.
formulas: Powers of 7 and 3 have period 4 modulo 10; powers of 4 alternate 4,6.
steps: 777≡1 (mod 4), so the first term ends in 7.
The even power of 14 ends in 6, and 333≡1 (mod 4) makes the last term end in 3.

problems.title: A custom operation is a squared sum
problems.question: Define a⊕b=a²+2ab+b². Evaluate (1⊕2)⊕(3⊕1).
problems.idea: Recognize the square identity.

problems.title: Substitute a common ratio unit
problems.question: If a/b=2/3, evaluate (3a-b)/(a+2b).
problems.idea: Write a=2t,b=3t, with t≠0.

problems.title: GCD uses the smaller prime exponents
problems.question: Find gcd(a,b) for a=2³3²7⁴,b=3³5²7².
problems.idea: Only common primes enter the gcd.

problems.title: A fraction as a percentage
problems.question: If a/b=2/3, what percentage of b is a?
problems.idea: Multiply the ratio by 100%.

problems.title: Convert both percentages to multipliers
problems.question: 20% of a equals 300% of b. Find a/b.
problems.idea: Write the equality without percent signs.

problems.title: Price changes apply to the current price
problems.question: A shop has 140 toys. It sells 2/7 at 25 lari, then 3/5 of the remainder after a 20% discount, then all remaining toys after a 20% rise. Find total revenue.
problems.idea: Track quantities and prices separately.
formulas: After -20% multiply by 0.8; after +20% multiply by 1.2.
steps: Day 1: 40 toys at 25 give 1000 lari; 100 remain.
Day 2: 60 toys at 20 give 1200 lari; 40 remain.
Day 3: the new price is 20·1.2=24, giving 40·24=960.

problems.title: A common divisor divides the difference
problems.question: What is the largest natural number by which (11n+3)/(11n+9) can be reduced for a positive integer n?
problems.idea: Any common divisor divides 6.
steps: The numerator and denominator differ by 6, so their gcd is at most 6.
At n=3 the fraction is 36/42, whose gcd is 6.

problems.title: An impossible line-intersection count
problems.question: Which listed number 1,2,3,4,5,6 cannot be the number of intersection points of four distinct lines?
problems.idea: Classify parallel and concurrent arrangements.
formulas: Four lines have at most C(4,2)=6 pairwise intersections.
steps: If a pair meets at P and all lines pass through P, there is only one intersection.

If three lines are concurrent and a fourth misses their common point, it meets at least two of them, giving at least three distinct points. If no three are concurrent, intersections are all distinct and the count is 6 minus the number of parallel pairs; the allowed parallel-class patterns give 0,3,4,5 or 6.
Thus 2 is impossible; all other listed counts occur.
problems.note: The question concerns four distinct lines and isolated intersection points; coincident lines would share infinitely many points.

problems.title: Both clock hands move
problems.question: Find the smaller angle between the clock hands at 10:54.
problems.idea: Use 6° per minute for the minute hand and 0.5° per minute for the hour hand.
steps: The minute hand is at 324° from 12.

problems.title: Crossing segments give opposite-side constraints
problems.question: A line crosses AG,HE,AC,EC,DG,FB,FH. Which listed four endpoints must be on the same side?
problems.idea: Crossing a line places the endpoints in opposite open half-planes.
formulas: Each crossing reverses the side assignment.
steps: Put A on side 1. Then G,C are on side 2.
EC puts E on side 1; HE puts H on side 2; DG puts D on side 1.
FH puts F on side 1 and FB puts B on side 2.

problems.title: Midpoints on a segment
problems.question: C,B lie inside NM, with B∈CN. CB=15,MN=55,MC=25. Find the distance between the midpoints of CB and NM.
problems.idea: Choose a coordinate from M toward N.

problems.title: The two unknown outer pieces enter only through their sum
problems.question: Rays OM,ON,OP,OQ occur in order. MOQ=70°,NOP=40°. Find the angle between the MON and POQ bisectors.
problems.idea: The outer two gaps total 30°.

problems.title: Two unequal transversal angles are supplementary
problems.question: For parallel lines cut by a transversal, three equal angles have sum 30% greater than two unequal angles. Find the difference of the unequal angles.
problems.idea: The unequal pair sums to 180°.
steps: Its supplement is 102°, and their difference is 24°.

problems.title: A percentage relation between supplementary angles
problems.question: 40% of one supplementary angle equals 50% of the other. Find their difference.
problems.idea: Translate the percentages to a ratio.

problems.title: Two adjacent supplementary angles
problems.question: An angle equals 10% of the sum of its two adjacent angles. Find it.
problems.idea: Each adjacent angle is the supplement of the original.

problems.title: Alternate exterior angles need not sum to 180 degrees
problems.question: Which listed statement about a transversal through parallel lines can be false?
problems.idea: Alternate exterior angles are equal, rather than always supplementary.
formulas: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; adjacent and same-side interior angles sum to 180°.
steps: If each alternate exterior angle is 60°, their sum is 120°, not 180°.
This supplies a counterexample to the proposed sum statement.
problems.answer: “Alternate exterior angles sum to 180°” can be false.

problems.title: Two ratio divisions leave one third between the rays
problems.question: OC lies inside AOE. OB splits AOC in ratio 2:1 from OA; OD splits EOC in ratio 2:1 from OE. BOD=20°. Find AOE.
problems.idea: The two gaps beside OC are each one third of their larger angle.

problems.title: Equal times give an arithmetic mean speed
problems.question: A car covers 432 km, half the time at 108 km/h and half at 72 km/h. Find total time.
problems.idea: The two time intervals are equal.

problems.title: Only perfect squares have an odd divisor count
problems.question: Which listed number 2204,2250,2254,2304,2400,2450 has an odd number of positive divisors?
problems.idea: Divisors usually pair as d and n/d.
formulas: An unpaired divisor exists exactly when d=√n is an integer.
steps: The other listed numbers are not perfect squares, so their divisor counts are even.
